newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on export prospects.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on export prospects.

text.p: Prospects for declining exports of U.S. corn including confirmation Taiwan would cut back on its imports pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.

USDA late Monday said Taiwan would import the smallest amount of corn in three years at 5.83 million tonnes, below the previous estimate for 6.33 million tonnes. An outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan led to the slide in feed needs by that Island.
Corn also was pressured by some talk about potential increases in U.S. sorghum acreage.
Signals some wheat acreage in the U.S. Great Plains was harmed by a weekend freeze led to ideas for abandonment of wheat acreage and a resultant shift into sorghum acreage.
Traders also said corn was in a technical slide and the early break in the wheat market helped tilt corn even lower by midsession.
But support held in the nearby May at the $3.00 per bushel market which was encouraging for the bull's case. The session low for May was $2.99 per bushel.
Corn futures closed one to 3-1/2 cents lower, with May down one at $3.02-3/4 per bushel.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 63,000 contracts, below the 73,099 traded Monday.

Cargill Inc bought five million bushels of December, Smith Barney bought five million bushels of July and LFG Futures sold three million bushels of May, traders said. Iowa Grain sold three million bushels of May and O'Connor and Co sold two two million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, O'Connor and Co did three million bushels of May/July at two cents, premium July, traders said.

In corn options, E.D. and F. Man International sold 400 May $2.90 puts at 1/2 cent, Term Commodities sold 500 May $2.90 puts at 1/2 cent and Paine Webber sold 400 July $3.30 calls at 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 17,081 traded Monday.
